x: K. Miller is a new member and shows every promise.
He does seem to be a most unlucky runner; in the Surrey Championship he went off course when in second position. Positions :- 22, K.
Black, following his unfortunate mishap at Epsom, ran well to finish 66th with K.

The Junior mile was won by a St.Mary's College runner in 4m.41.4s. with K.Miller 2nd and E.Penny 4th. We were short of good milers in the Senior event, Herne Hill again taking maximum points, with Bill Bird 3rd.

Whilst Geoff Stevens 118th, and K.Miller 1[illegible]6th improved on their Southern running our other lads found the pace too hot. No one was disgraced, however, and in them we have some good material for the future.
These hopes appeared to be well founded when, after a ½ mile, Alan was seen to be in third place, well backed up by Ken Miller and John Thresher in the early twenties and Trevor Hart in the sixties.
Alan Black, our best junior, was well down the field and only started to run over the last mile or two, when he made about seventy places. Individual positions:- 66, K.
We finished fourth to Victoria Park(58m.59s.), Thurruck H.(59.19) and Bramley (59.24) Individual times:- K.
Don MacLean, now running more like his old self, finished second in the two mile event to Hugh Foord with a time of 9m.33.8s: other places:- K.
Don MacLean was our fastest man in the 2 miles, finishing 3rd in 9m.56s..Our other runners were K. Miller (10m4s.) David Jones(10m.22s.) and Ted Pallent(10m.50s.)
